questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How much water we really need to drink
Why bottled water is better than tap water
How blood carries nutrients around the body
Why governments want people to drink less
questions.why: They discuss exactly how much water we need to stay healthy.

questions.q: What does Phil say about his own water drinking?
options: He drinks about two litres a day, which he thinks is too much for him
He never drinks water
He carries a water bottle everywhere
He drinks about a litre, but thinks two litres is recommended
questions.why: Phil says he drinks maybe about a litre and thinks you should drink about two.

questions.q: What does biologist Professor John Speakman say about the two-litre advice?
options: Only a few countries recommend it, and most scientists say it is too much
He doesn't know where it came from, but almost all governments give it
It was calculated by his university
It is only for athletes
questions.why: He's not sure how it was arrived at, but government recommendations around the world are 'pretty much all the same'.

questions.q: Is the figure of two litres based on scientific evidence?
options: Yes, it comes from many studies
Yes, but only for children
No, it's more of a rough estimate
No, scientists say we need much less
questions.why: Phil says it isn't based on scientific fact – it's more of a ballpark figure.

questions.q: Why does Beth compare the body to a bank balance?
options: To say that water is expensive
To explain why people save water
To show that the body is always losing water, which must be replaced
To show that everyone needs to drink exactly the same amount of water
questions.why: Like money spent from a bank account, the body keeps losing water when we breathe, sweat or use the toilet.

questions.q: According to Beth, what mainly decides how much water you need?
options: Your size
Your age
The weather
How much food you eat
questions.why: She says it depends on how much water your body needs to replace, which mainly depends on your size.

questions.q: What does hydration expert Dr Nidia Rodriguez-Sanchez say about dehydration?
options: It only happens in hot countries
It is very rare in adults
It always causes a dry mouth before any other signs
We often don't realise it is happening
questions.why: She says 'many times we start getting dehydrated and we don't realise'.

questions.q: What mistake does Dr Rodriguez-Sanchez say people sometimes make?
options: They drink too much coffee
They think they're hungry and eat, when they're actually thirsty
They drink water only at night
They think a headache means they need more sleep, so they go to bed early
questions.why: She says we may think we're hungry and get food, when 'actually… we are thirsty'.
